blogs.title: When Breath Is Lost: How Chiari Malformation Mimics ‘Ondine’s Curse’
blogs.description: Explores the pathophysiology of acquired central hypoventilation in Chiari I disease, differentiating it from congenital central hypoventilation and highlighting the clinical pearls that should prompt consideration of a structural brainstem disorder in patients with unexplained nocturnal desaturation or ‘silent’ choking spells.

blogs.title: Choking Without a Cast: Why Dysphagia Should Trigger a Neurologic Work‑up
blogs.description: Reviews the neurogenic vs mechanical causes of dysphagia, the significance of choking with both solids and liquids, and how persistent swallowing issues can be a harbinger of Chiari I. Includes practical guidance on when to refer for MRI and swallow physiology evaluation.

blogs.title: Lost in the Old CT: The Importance of Re‑reviewing Retrospective Imaging for Hidden Chiari
blogs.description: Discusses the diagnostic pitfalls of overlooking a crowded foramen magnum on routine head CTs, the role of image re‑analysis, and how history‑guided imaging reviews can uncover under‑diagnosed Chiari I, especially in patients with vague neuro‑symptoms spanning years.

blogs.title: Headache, Hair, and the Burning Vertex: Unraveling Occipital Neuralgia in Chiari I
blogs.description: Highlights the intriguing link between vertex allodynia, occipital neuralgia, and Chiari I. Covers current evidence, differential diagnosis, and practical management options (nerve blocks, hair length adjustment, pharmacologic therapies) for clinicians handling atypical scalp pain.

blogs.title: Sleep Studies for Chiari: Why Polysomnography Is Essential—and What Type‑III Misses
blogs.description: Analyzes the limitations of portable type‑III sleep studies in capturing central hypoventilation, the importance of full‑channel polysomnography with EEG and capnography, and how to interpret AHI and central event percentages in patients with posterior fossa compression.

blogs.title: From Trauma to Tonsillar Herniation: Understanding Primary vs Secondary Chiari I
blogs.description: Examines the emerging classification of Chiari malformations, the role of head trauma in precipitating or unmasking tonsillar descent, and what this means for screening, surveillance, and counselling of post‑trauma patients who may develop late‑onset neurological symptoms.
